names: Rainy Pass / Lake Ann–Maple Pass Trailhead
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at the Rainy Pass trailhead — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From the paved pullout at Rainy Pass (4,855 ft) on SR-20 — signed 'Rainy Pass Trailhead,' 52 miles east of Marblemount, right where the PCT crosses the highway — start on the Lake Ann/Maple Pass Trail (well-graded, heavily used).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District (Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness)
storedPass: A Northwest Forest Pass (or an Interagency/America the Beautiful Annual, Day, Senior, Access, or Military Pass) is required to park at the West Fork Buttermilk Trailhead — it appears on the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest's official list of day-use fee sites.
drive: From the West Fork Buttermilk Trailhead (elev. ~3,960 ft, at the end of FR-4300-500 off East Buttermilk Creek Road/FR-43, reached via Twisp River Road west of Twisp), follow the West Fork Buttermilk Trail #411 into the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.

names: SR 20 pullout (1.5 mi W of pass)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From Winthrop, drive west on SR-20 about 27 miles (about 4 miles east of Washington Pass), turn right onto Forest Road 400, and follow it about 1 mile to the trailhead parking.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required at developed trailheads.
drive: Via Beckler River Road (FR-65) into the FR-6510/6514/6517 spur network to road's end ~0.5 mile east of the summit. Since the December 2025 floods Eagle Creek Road (FR-6514) has been gated at its start and FR-6510 at milepost 1, so the road end cannot be reached by car right now.
From Leavenworth on US-2, turn onto Icicle Creek Road and follow it west to Eightmile Campground.

landManager: National Park Service / U.S. Forest Service
storedPass: None required — there are no trailhead or parking fees for trails that begin on National Park Service land.
drive: From Diablo (SR-20 milepost 126): park near the pool building; the Sourdough Mountain Trail starts behind it (~900 ft)

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Entiat Ranger District
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency (America the Beautiful) Pass, or pay the $5/day fee on-site.
drive: Start at the North Fork Entiat River Trailhead (~3,940 ft) at the end of Forest Road 5606, off Entiat River Road.

landManager: National Park Service — Mount Rainier National Park
storedPass: Standard Mount Rainier NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7 days), $55 Mount Rainier annual pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From the Nisqually Entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive to Longmire, pass the National Park Inn and turn right at the two-story building with the flagpole. Continue straight through the employee housing area and across the suspension bridge, which has a 3-ton vehicle limit; the trailhead is 300 feet past the bridge and parking is limited.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Cle Elum Ranger District
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful/Interagency Pass
drive: From the De Roux trailhead and campground on FR-9737, via the Boulder-De Roux Trail #1392 west up the valley to its last switchback

landManager: U.S. Forest Service — Glacier Peak Wilderness (approach partly crosses NPS Lake Chelan National Recreation Area)
storedPass: No parking pass reportedly required.
drive: Via the Lady of the Lake ferry (or floatplane) from Chelan to Stehekin Landing, then the shuttle ~4.4 miles to Harlequin Bridge and the Stehekin River Trail

names: Frenchman Coulee parking on Vantage Road
drive: From Seattle take Interstate 90 east over the Columbia River past Vantage to exit 143, turn left onto Silica Road, pass beneath the freeway, then turn left at the first chance onto Vantage Road and follow it 1.4 miles down the canyon to parking on the left. A Discover Pass is required. Since May 2026 rockslides have closed Vantage Road, so the parking cannot be reached by car; check the road status before you go.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Naches Ranger District) — Goat Rocks Wilderness
storedPass: Required at the Conrad Meadows trailhead — $5/day or $30/year Northwest Forest Pass.
drive: Drive to the Conrad Meadows / South Fork Tieton Trailhead (Trail #1120, elev. ~4,044 ft): from Naches, WA take US-12 W about 22 miles, turn onto Forest Road 1200 (Tieton Reservoir Road) for 4.5 miles, then onto Forest Road 1000 (South Fork Tieton Road) for 12.6 miles to the trailhead at road's end (last ~7 miles gravel, generally in good condition).

landManager: Gifford Pinchot National Forest (Cowlitz Valley Ranger District) — Goat Rocks Wilderness
storedPass: Required at both the Snowgrass Flat and Berry Patch trailheads — $5/day or $30/year Northwest Forest Pass.
drive: From US 12 about 3 miles before Packwood, turn south onto Forest Road 21 and follow the gravel road about 13 miles, take a slight left onto Forest Road 2150, then go less than 3 miles and turn right into the Snowgrass Flat Trailhead parking loop.
From the Mazama store, drive about 3.1 miles up Lost River Road to the Goat Wall Creek drainage and pull off nearby.

landManager: United States Forest Service (Olympic National Forest)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful Pass (depends on parking area)
drive: From the spur-270 pullout

landManager: Olympic National Park (Wilderness) for the summit ridge / Olympic National Forest – Buckhorn Wilderness, Quilcene Ranger District for the approach
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30 annual or $5 daily) required for trailhead parking; no Olympic National Park entrance fee applies here since the standard trailhead is on Olympic National Forest land, not inside the Park.

names: NF-6514-410 spur end (Beckler River road network)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required at developed trailheads.
drive: From the end of FS spur NF-6514-410 off Beckler River Road (FR-65). Since the December 2025 floods Eagle Creek Road (FR-6514) has been gated at its start, with a blown-out culvert beyond, so the spur cannot be reached by car right now.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: From Glacier, WA, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east and turn onto Forest Service Road 33; follow roughly 11 miles of gravel road (rough in sections, high-clearance/SUV recommended, sedans passable with care) to its end at the Cougar Divide Trailhead/parking (room for 8-10 vehicles).

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: From Glacier, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (Forest Road 39), turn right, then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (Forest Road 37) and follow it 12.7 miles to the trailhead at the end of the road. Since June 2026 Deadhorse Road has been closed at its start until further notice while flood damage is repaired; check the road status before you go.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest / Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: No fee/pass required at the Libby Lake Trailhead itself (undeveloped, no fee station or facilities).
drive: From Carleton, drive SR-153 south 1.4 miles, turn right onto Libby Creek Road for 2.5 miles, then left onto FR-43 for 5.1 miles. Turn left onto FR-4340 for 1.2 miles, right onto FR-700 for 1.5 miles, and left onto FR-750 for 0.9 mile to the trailhead.

names: Hozomeen Lake / Willow Lake trailhead at Hozomeen Campground
landManager: National Park Service — Ross Lake National Recreation Area, North Cascades National Park Complex. NPS complex information line 360-854-7200; Wilderness Information Center, Marblemount, 360-854-7245.

names: PCT Trailhead, Snoqualmie Pass (Exit 52, Alpental Rd)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Snoqualmie Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
drive: From I-90 take Exit 52; the trailhead is at the end of the gravel ski-area parking lot, reached by turning left under the freeway and taking the first right from the eastbound off-ramp, or by turning right and immediately right again from the westbound off-ramp.
From Leavenworth, drive Icicle Creek Road, reached from US-2, for about 6.5 miles; the pullout is on the right.

names: Hannegan Trailhead / Campground (Hannegan Pass Road, FR 32)
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District); Icy Peak's summit area within North Cascades National Park
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass (parking) / NPS backcountry permit (overnight camping in the Park)
drive: From Mount Baker Highway (SR-542), about 12.5 miles east of the Glacier Public Service Center, turn left onto Hannegan Pass Road (FR-32) and drive about 5.3 miles to the road-end trailhead.

names: Icicle Creek Road roadside parking (Hook Creek Drainage)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass recommended ($5 day pass or $30 annual)

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From the pullout where SR-20 crosses Silver Star Creek near milepost 171 (~3,450 ft), about 8.5 miles east of Washington Pass
In Spokane, drive to Canyon Drive and use the upper of the two parking lots.
